title: Measure the report delay before buying more capacity?
situation:
We send a daily sales report to 24 shops so managers can plan their morning orders. Reports normally arrive within 10 minutes of closing, and that was still true last week. Since Monday, the same reports have taken about 45 minutes. All 24 eventually arrived on each of the last three days, so we have evidence of delay, not missing sales data.

The slowdown began when we moved report generation to a shared queue. We do not yet know whether reports are waiting behind other jobs or taking longer to calculate once they start. That distinction determines whether buying more capacity would help.
impact: Managers now wait an extra 35 minutes before they can use the report. Two shops have told support that they placed orders without it. If the queue is the cause, changing when reports run could restore delivery without a recurring bill. If calculation itself is slower, moving the schedule would leave the underlying problem in place.

recommendation.action: Measure one daily report run before buying more capacity.
recommendation.why: Record the waiting time and calculation time separately tomorrow. This should tell us which change addresses the delay, using the timing tools we already have. The tradeoff is one more morning of slow reports while we gather evidence; we cannot promise recovery tomorrow.

alternatives.action: Add capacity now for an estimated $300 a month.
alternatives.consequence: It may reduce the delay immediately, but could leave us paying more while reports still wait behind other work.

if_no_answer: We will keep the current queue and capacity, and continue checking that every report arrives. The delay remains unresolved. Please choose before tomorrow’s run if you want the measurement step included; no purchase will happen without approval.
